title: Forces, initial data and Newtonian flow

items.title: Adopted force model: force maps, the equation of motion, additive composition of force contributions and frame covariance
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about
forces and motion, in the spacetime, frames and worldlines of
[[post-cm01-spacetime]], [[post-cm01-frames]] and [[post-cm01-worldlines]].

**(i) Setting and configuration domain.** A model of the framework has
$N\ge1$ particle labels with fixed positive masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}$
([[post-cm01-worldlines]], clause (v)) and a configuration domain $Q$ in one
fixed inertial frame, in the unconstrained branch of
[[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a): $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ is open,
possibly with the collision set $\Delta$ removed when the force law of the
model is singular at coincident positions. The constrained branch of that
definition, with its reaction forces, is **not** covered by this postulate; the
dynamics of constrained systems is a separate development with its own
assumptions. A **state** of the model is a pair $z=(x,v)\in Q\times\mathbb
R^{3N}$ of positions and coordinate velocities of the labels in the chosen
frame ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]).

**(ii) Time window.** A model carries a nondegenerate open interval
$I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, its **time window**, read in seconds
([[def-cm01-units]]).

**(iii) Force map and standing regularity.** A **force map** on this data is a
map

$$F:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\longrightarrow(\mathbb R^{3})^{N},\qquad (t,x,v)\longmapsto F(t,x,v)=\bigl(F_{1}(t,x,v),\dots,F_{N}(t,x,v)\bigr),$$

with components of dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$, read in newtons
([[def-cm01-units]]). The standing hypotheses of this branch, which every
force map of a model is required to satisfy, are:

1. **Continuity.** $F$ is continuous on its domain
   $D:=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$.
2. **State-local Lipschitz regularity, locally uniform in time.** $F$ is
   locally Lipschitz in the state variable $z=(x,v)$, locally uniformly in
   time, in the sense of [[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]: every
   compact cylinder $C\subseteq D$ carries a finite $L\ge0$ with
   $\lVert F(t,z)-F(t,z')\rVert_{2}\le L\lVert z-z'\rVert_{2}$ whenever
   $(t,z),(t,z')\in C$ share their time coordinate.

A map that fails clause 1 or clause 2 is **not** a force map of this branch,
whatever its other merits. When a later statement differentiates the force map
(for instance in a linearization or a smooth-dependence claim), it adds the
required differentiability hypothesis of the state variable explicitly; clause
2 alone licenses only the existence, uniqueness and continuation statements
proved on this page.

**(iv) Equation of motion.** Adopt: the motion of the labels of a model with
force map $F$ in an inertial frame is governed by

$$m_{i}\,\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),\dot x(t)\bigr)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N),$$

imposed along families of $C^{2}$ coordinate curves of the labels
$x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N}):J\to Q$, where $J\subseteq I_{0}$ is an interval with
nonempty interior and the derivatives are those of
[[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]. The precise notion of a motion of the
model, its associated first-order system and its maximal motions is
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. The force map is **primitive data** of the model:
the equations above are the model's law, not an operational definition of $F$
from a measured acceleration, and $F$ is not an extra observable measured
independently of the motion. The mass $m_{i}$ in (iv) is the fixed inertial
mass of clause (v) of [[post-cm01-worldlines]]; no other mass occurs in this
clause.

**(v) Additive composition of force contributions.** When a model presents its
force map as composed of contributions, the composition is the pointwise sum:
for force maps $F^{(1)},\dots,F^{(k)}$ on a common domain satisfying (iii),

$$F(t,z)=\sum_{a=1}^{k}F^{(a)}(t,z),$$

and the sum again satisfies (iii), because a finite sum of continuous maps is
continuous and a finite sum of maps that are locally Lipschitz in the state
variable is locally Lipschitz with a locally uniform constant. This
**superposition of forces** is an adopted modelling rule, not a theorem about
nature: it says how the model's total force is composed from the contributions
it declares. Two decompositions with the same sum define the same force map
and the same model; the framework does not measure an individual contribution
in isolation, and no observation of motions alone determines a decomposition.
Nor does (v) assert that sums of motions are motions: if $F$ is not affine in
the state, the sum of two solutions of (iv) generally does not satisfy (iv),
and superposing solutions is a separate question from superposing forces.

**(vi) Description in another inertial frame.** Let $F_{*}=\bigl(o',u',
(e_{1}',e_{2}',e_{3}')\bigr)$ be a second inertial frame related to the frame
of (i) by the Galilean transformation

$$t'=t+b,\qquad x_i'=Rx_i+\upsilon t+a_{0}\quad(i=1,\dots,N)$$

with $b\in\mathbb R$, $a_{0},\upsilon\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $R\in SO(3)$
([[pthm-cm01-galilean-kinematics]] clause 1;
[[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]); $\upsilon$ is the boost velocity
denoted by $v$ in that theorem. Define the block-diagonal map
$$R_{N}:=\operatorname{diag}(R,\dots,R):\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$$
and the repeated tuples $\bar a_{0}:=(a_{0},\dots,a_{0})$ and
$\bar\upsilon:=(\upsilon,\dots,\upsilon)$ in $(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$. Thus
$R_N x=(Rx_{1},\dots,Rx_{N})$, and the same componentwise rule applies to
velocities and forces; since $R^{\mathsf T}R=I_{3}$,
$R_N^{\mathsf T}R_N=I_{3N}$. If $x:J\to Q$ is a family of motions of the
labels in the first frame, then the description of the same worldlines in the second
frame is
$$\eta(t'):=R_{N}x(t'-b)+\bar\upsilon(t'-b)+\bar a_{0}\qquad(t'\in J+b).$$
By clause 2 of the cited theorem, each $\eta_i$ is $C^{2}$ and
$\eta_i''(t')=R\ddot x_i(t'-b)$, so along the motion
$$m_i\eta_i''(t')=R F_i\bigl(t'-b,x(t'-b),\dot x(t'-b)\bigr).$$

Adopt: the same interaction, read in the second frame, is represented on the
transferred data by the force map below. Let $P$ be the inverse affine
transfer from new-frame data to old-frame data,
$$P(t',y,w):=\bigl(t'-b,\,R_N^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar\upsilon(t'-b)-\bar a_{0}),\,R_N^{\mathsf T}(w-\bar\upsilon)\bigr).$$
Its preimage of the original domain is
$$D_{*}:=P^{-1}(D)=\{(t',y,w):P(t',y,w)\in D\};$$
it is open because $P$ is a homeomorphism and $D$ is open. Define
$$F_{*}:D_{*}\to(\mathbb R^{3})^{N},\qquad F_{*}(t',y,w):=R_N F\Bigl(t'-b,\ R_N^{\mathsf T}\bigl(y-\bar\upsilon(t'-b)-\bar a_{0}\bigr),\ R_N^{\mathsf T}(w-\bar\upsilon)\Bigr).$$
The map $F_{*}$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz in its state variable:
the transfer and its inverse are affine, and at fixed time they act linearly
on state differences; on compact time intervals their state Lipschitz
constants are uniform, so precomposition preserves the stated regularity of
$F$. The framework
formulates the equation of motion in every inertial frame; a rule that does
not transform by this law is a description tied to the frame in which it was
written, and the framework attaches no kinematic covariance to it. When
$Q=\mathbb R^{3N}$ — the case of the models of the companion page — the
transferred domain is again a product
$I_{0}'\times\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $I_{0}'=I_{0}+b$, and
$F_{*}$ is a force map in the sense of (iii); for a proper open $Q$ the
transferred position set $R_NQ+\bar\upsilon(t'-b)+\bar a_0$ may depend on
$t'$, and the equation is then read on that transferred set.

**(vii) What this branch excludes.** Impulsive forcing (a finite momentum
transfer at an instant is not a force map); Coulomb sliding friction, whose
expression contains the factor $v/\lvert v\rvert$ and is undefined at $v=0$;
static friction, which requires an inequality or a set-valued reaction model;
stochastic forcing; and forces that exist only as distributions. Each of these
requires its own stated model and solution notion, and none is covered by
(iii)–(iv). A singular force law is admissible on a configuration domain with
the singular configurations removed — for instance an inverse-square law on
the collision-excluded $Q$ of clause (i) — and what the removal of those
configurations implies for existence in time is stated by the continuation
theorem of this page.

**(viii) Status.** Clause (iii) states the hypotheses under which the theorems
of this page are proved; clause (iv) is the adopted law of motion; clauses (v)
and (vi) are the adopted composition and frame rules. Nothing here is deduced
from experiment, from a symmetry principle or from the uniqueness theory of
differential equations, and nothing here asserts that any physical
interaction is exactly of this form: the theorems of this page are conditional
consequences of the adopted model. The empirical significance of a concrete
model lies in fully specified model parameters and reported observations
compared with its predictions, and this postulate supplies neither.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it adopts the force-map data with their continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses, the equation of motion in every inertial frame, additive composition of declared contributions and the transformation rule under frame changes, and records what the branch excludes and does not claim.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the framework's force branch: force maps as continuous, state-locally-Lipschitz vector-valued maps on a time window, an open configuration domain and velocity space, the equation of motion $m_i\ddot x_i=F_i(t,x,\dot x)$ in every inertial frame, pointwise additivity of declared force contributions, and the transformation rule that a force law must satisfy under a change of inertial frame. The postulate excludes impacts, dry and static friction, stochastic and distributional forcing, and constraint reactions; it asserts no measured value, no conservation law and no claim that any physical interaction is exactly of this form.

items.title: Restricted interaction models: pair decompositions, antisymmetry and centrality options, potential forces and the gravitational branch
items.statement:
Adopt, whenever a model of the force branch [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]
invokes them, the following **restricted interaction assumptions**. Throughout,
the data $I_{0}$, $Q$, $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}$ and the force map $F$ are those of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], and a state writes $z=(x,v)$ with
$x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})\in Q$ and $v=(v_{1},\dots,v_{N})\in\mathbb R^{3N}$.

**(i) External-plus-pair decomposition.** The model's force map is presented as

$$F_{i}(t,z)=F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t,x_{i},v_{i})+\sum_{j\ne i}F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j}) \qquad(i=1,\dots,N),$$

where each $F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a single-label **external** force map and
each $F_{ij}$ (for $i\ne j$, an ordered pair) is a **pair** force map, all
defined on their stated open domains and satisfying the standing continuity
and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of clause (iii) of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with respect to the arguments they actually
depend on. This is a restriction of the model class: an arbitrary force map
$F$ of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] need not admit such a decomposition,
and the decomposition is part of the model's declaration, not a theorem. It is
relative to the declared set of labels: for a subsystem, a pair force to a
label outside the declared set appears as an external force, and no
antisymmetry or pairing property of the full system restricts that external
force.

**(ii) Optional pair assumptions.** In addition, a model may adopt, separately
or together, the following assumptions about a pair force $F_{ij}$:

1. **Antisymmetry (weak form of the third law).**
   $F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j})=-F_{ji}(t,x_{j},x_{i},v_{j},v_{i})$ for
   all arguments in the domain.
2. **Centrality.** $F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j})$ is parallel to
   $x_{i}-x_{j}$, i.e. lies in the real line spanned by $x_{i}-x_{j}$,
   whenever $x_{i}\ne x_{j}$.

The **strong form of the third law** means antisymmetry together with
centrality; centrality alone does not imply antisymmetry.

Each assumption is a further restriction of the model class and is adopted
only where invoked. Both are *sufficient* hypotheses used by later balance
statements, and neither is a consequence of the equation of motion: a
velocity-dependent pair force, or an interaction mediated by a field omitted
from the declared labels, need satisfy neither.

**(iii) Potential model.** A model may present its force map through a scalar
**potential** $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, read in joules ([[def-cm01-units]]), through the rule

$$F_{i}(t,z)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N),$$

the gradient being the Euclidean gradient in the position variable of each
label ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). This is a restriction of the force class:
only force maps that are the negative gradient of such a potential belong to
it. The same force map arises from every potential of the form
$U(t,x)+c(t)$ with a differentiable function $c$ of $t$ alone whenever
the declared $C^{2}$ regularity is retained. More generally, for each connected
component $C$ of $Q$ (a maximal connected subset), two $C^{2}$ potentials
for the same force differ by an independently chosen $C^{2}$ function
$c_C(t)$ on $I_0\times C$. A single time function suffices when $Q$ is
connected; openness alone does not require the constants on different
components to agree. The chosen normalization is part of any later energy
statement and is recorded with it, and no energy statement is made on this page.

**(iv) Pair and external potentials are examples, not the general form.**
When $U$ has the form

$$U(t,x)=\sum_{i}u_{i}(t,x_{i})+\sum_{i<j}u_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j})$$

with $C^{2}$ scalar functions $u_{i}$, $u_{ij}$ on the respective open
time-position domains, each with energy dimension, the decomposition (i)
holds with $F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t,x_i,v_i)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}u_{i}(t,x_i)$
and, for every $i<j$, both ordered-pair maps given by

$$F_{ij}(t,x_i,x_j,v_i,v_j)=-\nabla_{x_i}u_{ij}(t,x_i,x_j),\qquad F_{ji}(t,x_j,x_i,v_j,v_i)=-\nabla_{x_j}u_{ij}(t,x_i,x_j).$$

Here the two gradients differentiate the first and second position arguments,
respectively, of the same declared $u_{ij}$; no $u_{ji}$ is required. These
maps are independent of velocities. Differentiating the finite sum for $U$
with respect to $x_i$ collects exactly the external term and one term for
each $j\ne i$, giving (i). Antisymmetry is not asserted for a general pair
potential. Potentials of the still more special form
$u_{ij}=u_{ij}(t,\lvert x_{i}-x_{j}\rvert)$ are the **central pair
potentials**; these are examples, and no generality is claimed for any of
these subclasses. Forces with nontrivial velocity dependence, such as the drag model
[[post-cm02-drag]] with $c>0$, lie outside every potential model of this
clause; when $c=0$ that model is a constant force and has a potential.

**(v) Newtonian gravitational branch.** The model may adopt the pair potential

$$U_{ij}(x_{i},x_{j})=-\frac{G_{\mathrm N}\,m_{i}^{g}m_{j}^{g}}{\lvert x_{i}-x_{j}\rvert}$$

on the collision-excluded configuration domain ($x_{i}\ne x_{j}$ for all
$i\ne j$), where $G_{\mathrm N}>0$ is a constant of dimension
$\ell^{3}\mu^{-1}\tau^{-2}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]) and the numbers
$m_{1}^{g},\dots,m_{N}^{g}>0$ are **gravitational coupling parameters** of the
labels, primitive model data distinct from the inertial masses $m_{i}$ of the
equation of motion. By clause (iii) this potential supplies the attractive
inverse-square pair force
$F_{ij}=-G_{\mathrm N}m_{i}^{g}m_{j}^{g}\,(x_{i}-x_{j})/\lvert x_{i}-x_{j}\rvert^{3}$,
the content of the elementary differentiation
$\nabla_{x}\bigl(1/\lvert x-y\rvert\bigr)=-(x-y)/\lvert x-y\rvert^{3}$; a
concrete instance of that differentiation is verified on the companion page.
The adopted model satisfies the antisymmetry and centrality options of (ii)
where they are invoked.

**(vi) The mass identification is an empirical assumption.** The
identification

$$m_{i}^{g}=m_{i}\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$

of gravitational couplings with inertial masses is **not** part of clauses
(i)–(v) and is not a consequence of the equation of motion. It is an
additional empirical assumption, adopted only when a model states it, and it
is the subject of the weak equivalence principle; the sources record its
empirical support and its historical status, and this page records no
measurement. Likewise, the inverse-square form in (v) is an adopted law, not a
consequence of the force branch [[post-cm02-force-superposition]].

**(vii) Status.** Clauses (i)–(v) are adopted modelling assumptions that
restrict the force maps of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]; they add no
dynamics beyond that postulate, and every theorem of this page remains
conditional on these adopted hypotheses. The balances of momentum, angular
momentum and energy, when asserted later, are theorems with their own
hypotheses on this structure and are not made here.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it adopts the restricted interaction models (external-plus-pair decomposition, optional antisymmetry and centrality, potential forces, the gravitational pair potential with couplings distinct from inertial masses) and records the mass identification as a further empirical assumption.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of restricted interaction models inside the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: a decomposition of the total force into external single-label forces and pair forces, the optional pair assumptions of antisymmetry and centrality, the branch of force maps that come from a scalar potential with the Euclidean gradient, and the optional Newtonian gravitational pair-potential model with gravitational coupling parameters distinct from the inertial masses. The item asserts no law of nature, no measured value and no conservation law; the identification of gravitational and inertial mass is recorded as a further empirical assumption, not adopted.

items.title: The associated first-order system, motions, maximal motions and the Newtonian flow of a force model
items.statement:
Let a force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] be given: time window
$I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ nondegenerate and open, configuration domain
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ open ([[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a)),
fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), and a
force map $F$ with the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz
hypotheses of clause (iii) of that postulate.

**(a) State domain and inverse-mass operator.** The **state domain** of the
model is

$$D:=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N},$$

an open subset of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{6N}$; a point $(t,x,v)\in D$ is a
time together with the **state** $z=(x,v)$ of positions $x\in Q$ and coordinate
velocities $v\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ of the labels ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). The **inverse-mass operator** is the linear map

$$\mathsf M^{-1}:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \mathsf M^{-1}(u_{1},\dots,u_{N}):=\Bigl(\frac{u_{1}}{m_{1}},\dots,\frac{u_{N}}{m_{N}}\Bigr),$$

the inverse of the mass operator $\mathsf M$ of clause (d) of
[[def-cm01-configuration]].

**(b) Associated first-order system.** The **associated first-order field** of
the model is

$$\mathcal F:D\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \mathcal F(t,x,v):=\Bigl(v,\ \mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\Bigr),$$

and the **associated first-order system** is $z'=\mathcal F(t,z)$ on the open
domain $D$, in the sense of
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]; here
$z=(x,v)\in\mathbb R^{6N}$. The map $\mathcal F$ satisfies the
Picard–Lindelöf hypotheses of
[[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]]: it is continuous on
$D$, and it is locally Lipschitz in the state variable $z$ locally uniformly
in time, because its first component $z\mapsto v$ is linear and its second is
the composition of the force map $F$ — which is locally Lipschitz in $(x,v)$
locally uniformly in time by [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii) —
with the linear map $\mathsf M^{-1}$.

**(c) Motions.** Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior, endpoints read with one-sided derivatives as in
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. A **motion** of
the model on $J$ is a curve $x:J\to Q$ of class $C^{2}$ such that
$t\in I_{0}$ for every $t\in J$ and

$$m_{i}\,\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),\dot x(t)\bigr)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N,\ t\in J).$$

Equivalently: the state curve $z=(x,\dot x):J\to D$ is a solution of the
associated first-order system on $J$. Indeed, if $x$ is a motion then
$z=(x,x')$ is $C^{1}$ with
$z'=(x',x'')=(x',\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,x'))=\mathcal F(t,z)$ and $z(t)\in D$;
conversely, if $z=(x,v)$ is a solution with $z(t)\in D$ for all $t$, then
$x'=v$ and $v'=\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)$, so $v$ is $C^{1}$, $x$ is $C^{2}$, and
multiplying the second equation by the masses returns the displayed
second-order equation. Motions of the labels of the model are exactly these
curves by [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iv).

**(d) Initial data and maximal motion.** An **initial datum** of the model is
a triple $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ with $t_{0}\in I_{0}$, $x_{0}\in Q$ and
$v_{0}\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$; write $z_{0}:=(x_{0},v_{0})$. A **maximal
motion** with this datum is a motion $x:J_{\max}\to Q$ with $x(t_{0})=x_{0}$
and $\dot x(t_{0})=v_{0}$ that has no extension to a motion of the model on a
strictly larger interval. By the Picard–Lindelöf hypotheses verified in (b)
and the maximal-solution theorem
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution]] (with
[[def-maximal-ode-solution]]): every initial datum has exactly one maximal
motion, its **maximal interval** $J_{\max}$ is an open interval containing
$t_{0}$ and contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion with the same datum is the
restriction of the maximal one. The restriction statement transfers from the
associated first-order system to motions through the equivalence in (c).

**(e) Newtonian flow.** The **Newtonian flow** of the model is the map

$$\Phi:\Omega\longrightarrow Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \Omega:=\bigl\{(t,t_{0},z_{0}):t_{0}\in I_{0},\ z_{0}\in Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\ t\in J_{\max}(t_{0},z_{0})\bigr\},$$

defined by $\Phi(t;t_{0},z_{0}):=z(t)$, where $t\mapsto z(t)=(x(t),\dot x(t))$
is the state curve of the maximal motion with datum $(t_{0},z_{0})$. By (d) the
assignment is well defined: the maximal motion is unique, so $\Phi$ is a
function on $\Omega$ and not merely a relation. For fixed $t_{0}$ and $z_{0}$
the curve $t\mapsto\Phi(t;t_{0},z_{0})$ is defined exactly on the maximal
interval $J_{\max}(t_{0},z_{0})$.
items.strategy: A definition: it fixes the state domain, the inverse-mass operator, the associated first-order field and system, motions and their equivalence with the second-order equation, initial data, the maximal motion and its maximal interval (existence by the cited maximal-solution theorem), and the Newtonian flow map; regularity of the flow is left to separate results.
items.physical_scope: Vocabulary of the force branch: the state space of positions and velocities, the inverse-mass operator, the associated first-order system of the second-order equation of motion, motions as its solutions, initial data, the maximal motion and its maximal interval, and the Newtonian flow map. The item defines objects only; it asserts no force law beyond the cited postulate, no regularity of the flow beyond what the cited existence theorems provide, and no empirical claim.

Adopt the force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: time window
$I_{0}$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, and a force map $F$ continuous and locally Lipschitz in
the state variable, locally uniformly in time, on
$D=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$. Let
$\mathcal F(t,x,v)=\bigl(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\bigr)$ be the associated
first-order field and let motions and maximal motions be as in
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. Fix an initial datum
$(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ and write
$z_{0}=(x_{0},v_{0})$.

1. **Local existence.** There is $h>0$ and there is a motion $x$ of the model
   on $[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$ with $x(t_{0})=x_{0}$ and $\dot x(t_{0})=v_{0}$;
   moreover such a motion is exactly one of class $C^{2}$ satisfying
   $m_{i}\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}(t,x(t),\dot x(t))$ for all $i$ and all
   $t\in[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$.
2. **Uniqueness.** If $x:J\to Q$ and $\tilde x:\tilde J\to Q$ are motions of
   the model with the same initial datum,
   $x(t_{0})=\tilde x(t_{0})=x_{0}$ and $\dot x(t_{0})=\dot{\tilde x}(t_{0})=v_{0}$,
   then $x=\tilde x$ on $J\cap\tilde J$.
3. **Quantitative cylinder.** Let $h,r>0$ satisfy
   $C:=[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]\times\overline B(z_{0},r)\subseteq D$, put
   $M:=\sup\{\lVert\mathcal F(t,z)\rVert_{2}:(t,z)\in C\}$ and let $\Lambda$
   be a state-Lipschitz constant of $\mathcal F$ on $C$. If $hM\le r$ and
   $\Lambda h<1$, then there is exactly one motion on $[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$
   through the datum whose state graph $(t,(x(t),\dot x(t)))$ lies in $C$, and
   every motion through the datum agrees with it on the intersection of its
   interval with $[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$.
4. **Maximal motion.** There is exactly one maximal motion with the datum:
   its maximal interval $J_{\max}$ is an open interval containing $t_{0}$ and
   contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion with the datum is its restriction.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force model: clause 1 locates a
solution only near $t_{0}$ and bounds no interval length in terms of the data,
clause 4 asserts no completeness of $J_{\max}$ in $I_{0}$, and no empirical
content is claimed.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: verify that the associated first-order field is continuous and locally Lipschitz on the open state domain, apply Picard-Lindelof in its quantitative cylinder form, translate the solution back to the second-order motion, prove uniqueness on common intervals, and obtain the unique maximal motion by the maximal-solution theorem.
items.physical_scope: The local existence, uniqueness and maximal-extension statement for the adopted Newtonian force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] on an open configuration domain: every initial datum with a configuration in the domain and an arbitrary coordinate velocity admits a unique motion through it, locally in time, and there is a unique maximal motion of which every motion with that datum is a restriction. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force postulate and the cited mathematical ODE theorems; it gives no global existence, no bound on the interval, no empirical statement and no claim that any physical system realizes the model.

items.title: Maximal Newtonian motions and the compact-continuation criterion: finite-time breakdown requires escape from every compact subset of the time-state domain
items.statement:
Adopt the force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with time window
$I_{0}$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and force map $F$ continuous and locally Lipschitz in the
state variable, locally uniformly in time; let $D=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb
R^{3})^{N}$, $\mathcal F(t,x,v)=\bigl(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\bigr)$,
$U:=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, and let motions, maximal motions and the state
curve $z=(x,\dot x)$ be as in [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. Fix an initial datum
$(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$, write
$z_{0}=(x_{0},v_{0})$, and let $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ be the maximal motion
with this datum, with state curve $z=(x_{\max},\dot x_{\max}):J_{\max}\to U$
and $J_{\max}=(a,b)$ its maximal interval, $-\infty\le a<b\le+\infty$.

1. **Existence and uniqueness of the maximal motion.** $J_{\max}$ is an open
   interval containing $t_{0}$ and contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion with
   the datum is a restriction of $x_{\max}$.
2. **Breakdown criterion.** If $b<+\infty$, then for every compact
   $K\subseteq D$ and every $\eta>0$ with $(b-\eta,b)\cap J_{\max}\neq\varnothing$
   there is $t\in(b-\eta,b)\cap J_{\max}$ with $(t,z(t))\notin K$. Equivalently:
   if there are a compact $K\subseteq D$ and $\delta>0$ with
   $(t,z(t))\in K$ for all $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap J_{\max}$, then
   $x_{\max}$ extends to a motion of the model on a strictly larger interval
   than $J_{\max}$ — so $J_{\max}$ cannot have right endpoint $b$.
3. **Autonomous case.** Suppose $F$ does not depend on its time argument:
   $F(t,x,v)=F_{0}(x,v)$ for a map $F_{0}:U\to(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ satisfying
   the standing regularity of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii).
   Then the associated field is autonomous,
   $\mathcal F(t,x,v)=(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F_{0}(x,v))$, the equations do not use
   the time coordinate, and **the model is read on the extended time window
   $\mathbb R$** (the standing hypotheses are unchanged by the extension).
   For this clause, take the same autonomous force law as a model on the
   extended time window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, and let $J_{\max}=(a,b)$ be the
   maximal interval for that extended-time model. If $b<+\infty$ and there
   are a compact $K_{0}\subseteq U$ and $\delta>0$ with $z(t)\in K_{0}$ for
   all $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap J_{\max}$, then the state curve extends past
   $b$ as a solution of the same model, contradicting maximality; thus no
   finite maximal endpoint has such a terminal compact trap. In particular,
   if one compact $K_{0}\subseteq U$ contains $z(t)$ for every
   $t\in J_{\max}\cap[t_{0},+\infty)$, then $b=+\infty$ and the motion is
   defined for all forward times $t\ge t_{0}$.
4. **Reading.** Suppose the time window is all of $\mathbb R$ (the
   time-dependent case included) and $b<+\infty$. Then for every compact
   $K_{0}\subseteq U$ and every $\delta>0$ there is $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap J_{\max}$ with
   $z(t)\notin K_{0}$: near a finite breakdown the state leaves every compact
   subset of the open state domain $U=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$. Consequently
   either the state is unbounded on every terminal interval, meaning that for
   every $M,\delta>0$ some $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap J_{\max}$ has
   $\lVert z(t)\rVert_{2}>M$, or $Q\ne\mathbb R^{3N}$ and the positions
   approach the excluded configurations in the following sense: for every
   $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ there are $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap J_{\max}$ and
   $y\in\mathbb R^{3N}\setminus Q$ with
   $\lVert x_{\max}(t)-y\rVert_{2}<\varepsilon$. If $Q=\mathbb R^{3N}$, the
   unbounded-state alternative necessarily holds.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction from the compact-continuation and escape theorems applied to the associated first-order system: a maximal motion with a finite endpoint leaves every compact subset of the open state domain, the autonomous case extends past a trapped endpoint, and the reading clause records the unbounded-state or excluded-configuration alternatives.
items.physical_scope: The continuation and breakdown criterion for the adopted Newtonian force model: the maximal motion of an initial datum is unique; at a finite right endpoint its time-state graph leaves every compact subset of the open time-state domain. On the extended time window R, the state leaves every compact subset of the open state domain; equivalently, it is unbounded on every terminal interval or, if it is bounded on some terminal interval and Q is proper, positions approach the excluded configurations in the explicitly stated sense. A finite right boundary of a finite time window is a separate possible endpoint. An autonomous force whose state is trapped in a compact subset of the state domain extends past the putative endpoint. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force postulate and the cited mathematical continuation theorems; it asserts no global existence for particular force laws, no empirical statement and no claim that any physical system realizes the model.

items.title: The uniform-force model: explicit global motion of a label under a constant declared field, with uniqueness, dimensions and frame covariance
items.statement:
Work in the force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N$ labels,
time window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3N}$, fixed
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, and fix a vector
$\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with dimension $[\mathbf g]=\ell\tau^{-2}$,
read in metres per second squared ([[def-cm01-units]]); $\mathbf g$ is a
**declared parameter** of the model, not a measured value. The **uniform-force
model** is the force map

$$F_{i}(t,x,v):=m_{i}\,\mathbf g\qquad(i=1,\dots,N),$$

constant in the state, so that every label has the same coordinate
acceleration $\mathbf g$ independently of its mass, position and velocity
([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]). Verify the following:

1. $F$ satisfies the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses
   of clause (iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]], with state-Lipschitz
   constant $0$ on every cylinder.
2. For the initial datum $x(0)=x_{0}$, $\dot x(0)=v_{0}$ the explicit curve,
   defined for every $t\in\mathbb R$,

   $$x_i(t)=x_{0,i}+v_{0,i}t+\tfrac12\mathbf g\,t^{2}\quad(i=1,\dots,N),\qquad x(t):=(x_1(t),\dots,x_N(t)).$$

   is a motion of the model on the whole time window $\mathbb R$ and is the
   unique maximal motion with this datum; its restriction to $[0,\infty)$ is
   therefore also a motion.
3. The dimension bookkeeping of the terms is consistent: the parameter has
   dimension length per time squared, the force components have dimension
   $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$, and the quadratic term has dimension length.
4. Under a change of inertial frame the model is covariant: in the second
   frame the same interaction is again a uniform-force model with parameter
   $\mathbf g'=R\mathbf g$, $R\in SO(3)$.
items.strategy: A worked verification: check the constant force map against the standing hypotheses with Lipschitz constant 0, verify the explicit quadratic motion and its initial data by differentiation, conclude uniqueness and global maximality from the initial-value theorem, and compute the dimension and frame-covariance statements.
items.physical_scope: A worked verification inside the framework: for one labeled particle of the model, the force map that assigns to every state the same vector $m\mathbf g$ (a declared constant field parameter of dimension length per time squared) satisfies the standing hypotheses of the force postulate; the explicit quadratic motion solves the initial-value problem, exists on the whole time window, is the unique maximal motion, and the model is covariant under changes of inertial frame with the parameter transforming as a spatial vector. The item is a computation inside the model: it asserts no measured value of any field strength, no property of the Earth's gravitational field and no empirical law, and the constant-field idealization is recorded as an approximation.

items.title: The linear drag model: a phenomenological velocity-proportional resistance with a declared coefficient
items.statement:
**(i) Setting.** Work in the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with one labeled particle of fixed mass
$m>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)) in a fixed inertial frame, with
time window $\mathbb R$ and configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, and with
the particle's coordinate position $x$ and coordinate velocity
$v=\dot x$ ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]). The particle moves through a
**medium** that fills the region of the motion and is at rest in the chosen
frame. The medium is not one of the model's particle labels, so its effect on
the label is an **external force** of the model in the sense of clause (i) of
[[post-cm02-interactions]]: the decomposition into the label's own dynamics
and the medium's effect is part of the model's declaration.

**(ii) The model.** Adopt as a **constitutive model** of the medium's net
force the **linear drag model** with a declared coefficient
$c\ge0$ of dimension $\mu\tau^{-1}$, read in kilograms per second
([[def-cm01-units]]):

$$F^{\mathrm{drag}}(v):=-c\,v,$$

optionally combined, through the additive composition of clause (v) of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], with a declared constant applied force
$m\mathbf g$, where $\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^{3}$ is a constant parameter of
dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). The resulting force map of the
model is

$$F(t,x,v)=m\mathbf g-c\,v,\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad m\,\ddot x=m\mathbf g-c\,\dot x,$$

the equation of a label whose only interactions are the constant applied field
and the linear resistance of the medium. The model is defined for all
$(t,x,v)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}\times\mathbb R^{3}$.

**(iii) Regularity.** The force map is affine in the state: it is continuous;
and for two states $z=(x,v)$, $z'=(x,v')$ sharing a position,
$\lVert F(t,z)-F(t,z')\rVert_{2}=c\,\lVert v-v'\rVert_{2}\le c\,\lVert z-z'\rVert_{2}$,
so it is locally Lipschitz in the state variable with the global constant $c$,
uniformly in time ([[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]). It is
therefore a force map of the branch [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause
(iii), and the existence, uniqueness and continuation theorems of this page
apply to it; the regularity check is recorded with the model checks on the
companion page.

**(iv) Physical status and regime.** This is a **phenomenological**
constitutive model, adopted rather than derived: it represents the net effect
of a medium whose microscopic state is not modelled, and the coefficient $c$
is a model parameter that depends on the body and the medium. The linear form
is a restricted regime — slow motion through a viscous medium, of which the
Stokes force on a sphere, $c=6\pi\eta a$ for dynamic viscosity $\eta$ and
radius $a$, is the recorded example — and other regimes are **different
models**: a force growing quadratically in the speed at higher speeds, or
Coulomb sliding friction, whose expression contains the factor
$v/\lvert v\rvert$ and is undefined at $v=0$, and which is outside clause
(iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] altogether. The model also neglects
the random component of the environment's force. The cited fluctuation
qualification is specifically Likharev's damped harmonic oscillator model
$m\ddot q+\gamma\dot q+\kappa q=0$, with $m,\kappa>0$ and damping coefficient
$\gamma>0$ (denoted $\eta$ in the source), oscillator energy
$E:=\tfrac12m\dot q^{2}+\tfrac12\kappa q^{2}$, and natural angular frequency
$\omega_{0}:=\sqrt{\kappa/m}$: footnote 4 says
that neglecting its random-force component is admissible only when, at thermal
equilibrium, $E$ is much greater than $\max(k_{\mathrm B}T,\hbar\omega_{0}/2)$,
where $T$ is temperature, $k_{\mathrm B}$ is Boltzmann's constant and $\hbar$
is the reduced Planck constant. The free-particle model stated here has no
restoring term and defines no corresponding $E$, $T$ or $\omega_{0}$, so the
oscillator condition is not an additional admissibility condition on this
model. Applying the idealization to a concrete medium requires a separate
model of its fluctuations.
No value of $c$, of $m$, or of $\mathbf g$ is asserted by this item, and using
measured values for them is an empirical premise with its own conditions and
uncertainty.

**(v) Status.** Adopted assumption of the framework when a model invokes it;
it selects no law of nature on its own and proves nothing about the actual
motion of any body in any medium. Its consequences within the model are the
subject of the companion example on terminal-velocity approach.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it adopts the linear drag force with a declared coefficient as a phenomenological model of a medium, records its regularity, its regime restrictions (linear/Stokes regime, quadratic and Coulomb friction as different models), the neglected environment fluctuations and the empirical status of its parameters.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of a constitutive force model for the interaction of a labeled particle with a medium: a linear drag force $-c\dot x$ with a declared coefficient $c\ge0$, optionally combined with a constant applied force. The model is phenomenological and restricted: it is adopted for a stated regime (slow motion in a viscous medium, the range in which the linear/Stokes form is used), its coefficient is a model parameter depending on body and medium, and the model neglects the random component of the environment's force. The item asserts no measured value, no derivation of the coefficient from the equation of motion, and no claim that the model applies to a given real motion.

items.title: Status audit and model boundaries of the force page: open systems, frame selection, breakdown and empirical scope
items.statement:
This remark records the status of the notions of the force page. It is
bookkeeping: it asserts no law and no empirical claim, and every mathematical
statement it repeats is proved in the item cited.

**Adopted assumptions.** The force branch is the postulate
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: the force map with its standing continuity
and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses, the equation of motion
$m_{i}\ddot x_{i}=F_{i}(t,x,\dot x)$, the additive composition of declared
force contributions, and the transformation rule under a change of inertial
frame. The restricted interaction models — external-plus-pair decompositions,
the optional antisymmetry and centrality assumptions, potential forces and the
gravitational pair-potential branch with its coupling parameters — are the
postulate [[post-cm02-interactions]]. The linear drag model, with its declared
coefficient and its regime and fluctuation qualifications, is the postulate
[[post-cm02-drag]].

**Defined objects.** The associated first-order system, motions, initial data,
maximal motions and the Newtonian flow are the definition
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]; the configuration domain, the mass operator and
the collision exclusion are [[def-cm01-configuration]], and the units and
dimensions read throughout are [[def-cm01-units]].

**Conditional deductions.** Local existence, uniqueness and the existence of
the maximal motion are [[pthm-cm02-ivp]]; the maximal-extension and breakdown
criterion, including the autonomous trapping statement, is
[[pthm-cm02-continuation]]. Both are conditional on the adopted force branch
and the cited mathematical ODE theorems; neither asserts that any physical
system realizes the model.

**Computed examples.** The uniform-force model with its explicit quadratic
motion, its uniqueness and its frame covariance is
[[ex-cm02-uniform-field]]. The companion page carries the worked model checks,
the projectile computation, the terminal-velocity computation and the two
counterexamples (nonuniqueness under a merely continuous force, and a singular
collision with finite breakdown time).

**Deliberately not claimed on this page.** No conservation law (momentum,
angular momentum, energy) is asserted: such statements require their own
hypotheses on the interaction structure and belong to later pages. No
constraint reactions and no constrained dynamics are adopted. No global
existence theorem for all force maps is claimed; the maximal interval may end
at a finite time. No measured value of any mass, field strength, drag
coefficient or gravitational coupling is asserted, and no comparison with
reported data is performed.
items.strategy: A scope remark: it audits the page status (adopted postulates, defined flow, proved theorems, computed example), states the open-system boundary between declared labels and environment, notes frame selection by external fields and apparatus, and records the regularity, breakdown and empirical scope cautions of the page.
items.physical_scope: A scope and status audit of the force page: which objects are adopted model data, which statements are conditional deductions, which computations are examples, and which claims are deliberately not made; the boundary between the declared particle labels and their environment in an open-system description; the way external fields and apparatus can provide a preferred descriptive frame or spatial location; the empirical status of force-law parameters, drag regimes and model comparisons. Bookkeeping and scope only; it asserts no law, no measurement and no claim about nature beyond the items it cites.

items.title: Standing regularity of the page's force models checked: uniform field, linear drag and the inverse-square model on its collision-excluded domain
items.statement:
Consider three force maps for a single label of mass $m>0$ in a fixed inertial
frame, each on the state domain indicated, with the standing hypotheses of
clause (iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] in view
([[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]):

1. **Uniform field.** $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, $F(t,x,v)=m\mathbf g$ for a declared
   constant $\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^{3}$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$
   ([[def-cm01-units]]).
2. **Linear drag with constant applied force.** $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$,
   $F(t,x,v)=m\mathbf g-c\,v$ with $c\ge0$ of dimension $\mu\tau^{-1}$
   ([[post-cm02-drag]]).
3. **Inverse-square external model.** $Q=\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$,
   $F(x)=-k\,x/\lvert x\rvert^{3}$ with $k>0$ of dimension
   $\mu\ell^{3}\tau^{-2}$, the force supplied by the external potential
   $U(x)=-k/\lvert x\rvert$ of the potential branch
   [[post-cm02-interactions]].

Verify: each map is continuous on its domain and locally Lipschitz in the
state variable, locally uniformly in time, with the explicit constants
$L=0$ for model 1, $L=c$ for model 2 and, on each annulus
$r\le\lvert x\rvert\le R$ inside $\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$,
$L=k\bigl(r^{-3}+3R^{3}r^{-6}\bigr)$ for model 3; and the inverse-square map
has no continuous extension to the excluded point $0$. Consequently the local
existence and uniqueness theorem [[pthm-cm02-ivp]] and the continuation
theorem [[pthm-cm02-continuation]] apply to each of the three models on its
stated domain.
items.strategy: A worked verification: check continuity and exhibit explicit state-Lipschitz constants for the uniform-field (0), linear drag (c) and inverse-square models, prove the local Lipschitz bound on collision-free annuli by an elementary norm estimate, show the inverse-square map has no continuous extension to the excluded center, and conclude that the ivp and continuation theorems apply to each model.
items.physical_scope: A worked model check inside the framework: verification that three force maps of this page satisfy the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of the force postulate, with explicit constants where available; the uniform-force model has constant 0, the linear drag model has constant c, and the inverse-square external model is locally Lipschitz on each collision-free annulus with the stated constant and has no continuous extension to the excluded center. The item is a finite verification inside the adopted models; it asserts no motion, no measurement and no empirical claim.

items.title: Projectile motion in the constant-field model: planar parabolic trajectory, flight time and level range for stated model data
items.statement:
Fix an inertial frame $(o,u,(b_1,b_2,b_3))$ and its adapted coordinates
as in [[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]. Write
$e_1=(1,0,0)$, $e_2=(0,1,0)$ and $e_3=(0,0,1)$ for the standard
coordinate basis of $\mathbb R^3$. Throughout, $x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$
is the coordinate position curve, with coordinate velocity $\dot x$ and
coordinate acceleration $\ddot x$; its associated worldline is
$\gamma(t)=o+tu+\sum_{j=1}^3x_j(t)b_j$, and its spatial displacement from
the frame origin at time $t$ is $\sum_jx_j(t)b_j\in K$, where $K$ is the
spatial displacement space of that definition.

Work in the constant-field model of [[ex-cm02-uniform-field]] with one label
of mass $m>0$, time window $\mathbb R$, configuration domain
$Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, and declared field parameter

$$\mathbf g=-g\,e_{3},\qquad g>0,\qquad [g]=\ell\tau^{-2}$$

([[def-cm01-units]]), so that the force map is $F(t,x,v)=m\mathbf g$ and the
equation of motion is $\ddot x(t)=-g\,e_{3}$. Fix the initial datum

$$x(0)=0,\qquad \dot x(0)=v_{0}\bigl(\cos\alpha\,e_{1}+\sin\alpha\,e_{3}\bigr), \qquad v_{0}>0,\qquad 0<\alpha<\pi/2 .$$

Verify: the unique maximal motion through the datum is

$$x(t)=\bigl(v_{0}\cos\alpha\bigr)t\,e_{1} +\Bigl(v_{0}\sin\alpha\,t-\tfrac12g\,t^{2}\Bigr)e_{3},$$

its trajectory lies in the plane $\operatorname{span}(e_{1},e_{3})$, and for
this model the return-to-launch-height time and the level range are

$$T_{\mathrm f}=\frac{2v_{0}\sin\alpha}{g},\qquad R_{\mathrm{range}}=\frac{v_{0}^{2}\sin(2\alpha)}{g}.$$

The level range and flight time are model quantities computed from the
declared parameters: no measured value of $g$, $v_{0}$ or $\alpha$ is
asserted, no medium and no drag are included, and the constant-field
description of a realistic field is an approximation recorded with the model.

items.title: Motion under linear drag and a constant applied force: explicit global solution and approach to the terminal velocity
items.statement:
Work in the linear drag model of [[post-cm02-drag]] with one label of mass
$m>0$, coefficient $c>0$, time window $\mathbb R$, configuration domain
$Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, and a declared constant vector
$\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^{3}$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$, so that the force
map is $F(t,x,v)=m\mathbf g-c\,v$ and the equation of motion is

$$m\,\ddot x(t)=m\,\mathbf g-c\,\dot x(t).$$

Define the **terminal velocity**

$$v_{\infty}:=\frac{m}{c}\,\mathbf g,\qquad [v_{\infty}]=\ell\tau^{-1},$$

and fix the initial datum $x(0)=x_{0}$, $\dot x(0)=v_{0}$. Verify:

1. the explicit curve

   $$x(t)=x_{0}+v_{\infty}t+\frac{m}{c}\bigl(v_{0}-v_{\infty}\bigr) \bigl(1-e^{-ct/m}\bigr)$$

   is a motion of the model on $\mathbb R$ with the stated datum, and by
   uniqueness it is the maximal motion;
2. its velocity satisfies
   $\dot x(t)=v_{\infty}+\bigl(v_{0}-v_{\infty}\bigr)e^{-ct/m}$ for all $t$,
   so that
   $\lvert\dot x(t)-v_{\infty}\rvert_{2}\le\lvert v_{0}-v_{\infty}\rvert_{2}\,e^{-ct/m}$
   and $\dot x(t)\to v_{\infty}$ as $t\to+\infty$: the velocity approaches the
   terminal velocity exponentially in time.
items.strategy: A worked computation: reduce the vector drag equation to scalar damped-oscillator equations with k=0, verify the explicit global solution by differentiation, conclude uniqueness and maximality, and estimate the exponential approach of the velocity to the terminal velocity with a direct epsilon argument.
items.physical_scope: A worked computation inside the linear drag model of [[post-cm02-drag]] with a constant applied force: for a stated initial position and velocity the explicit motion is verified, it is the unique maximal motion and exists for all real times, and its velocity converges to the terminal velocity $(m/c)\mathbf g$ with an explicit exponential bound. The item is a conditional computation inside the model; the coefficient and field parameters are declared model data, no measured value is asserted, and the phenomenological and regime qualifications of the drag postulate are preserved.

items.title: Continuity of the force map alone does not give unique motions: two distinct Newtonian motions through one datum for $F=\lambda\sqrt{|x_1|/\ell_*}\,e_1$
items.statement:
Consider the framework's equation of motion with one label of unit mass
($m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, [[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, and a force map
$F:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}\times\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ with
force components of dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]) that is
**merely continuous** — that is, the standing hypotheses of clause (iii) of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with the state-local-Lipschitz requirement
dropped. Then for every initial datum $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ there is at most
one motion of the model through that datum, on every interval containing
$t_{0}$.
items.strategy: A direct refutation: exhibit the continuous unit-mass force map F(x)=m sqrt(|x_1|) e_1 and two distinct C^2 motions through the rest datum (zero and a quartic-profile motion), verify the equation by differentiation, and record that the map fails exactly the state-local-Lipschitz clause, so the framework uniqueness theorem is unaffected.
items.physical_scope: A refutation, inside the framework's equation of motion, of the claim that a merely continuous force map suffices for uniqueness through an initial datum: the unit-mass model in three dimensions with force $F(x)=\lambda\sqrt{|x_{1}|/\ell_{*}}e_{1}$, where $[\lambda]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$ and $[\ell_*]=\ell$, is continuous but not state-locally-Lipschitz at the origin and exhibits two distinct $C^{2}$ motions through the rest datum. The item refutes only the weakened variant of the force postulate in which continuity replaces the local-Lipschitz clause; it asserts no motion of any physical body, no measurement and no empirical claim.

items.title: An external-source singularity reached in finite time: the inverse-square external model has a motion whose maximal interval is bounded above
items.statement:
Let $m>0$ and $k>0$ have dimensions $[m]=\mu$ and
$[k]=\mu\ell^{3}\tau^{-2}$, respectively ([[def-cm01-units]]). Consider the
force model of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] for one label with time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, external-source-excluded configuration domain
$Q=\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a)), mass
$m$, and the external potential

$$U(x)=-\frac{k}{\lvert x\rvert},\qquad U:Q\to\mathbb R,$$

of the potential branch of [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (iii), so that the
force map is $F(x)=-\nabla U(x)=-k\,x/\lvert x\rvert^{3}$ and the equation of
motion is

$$m\,\ddot x(t)=-\frac{k\,x(t)}{\lvert x(t)\rvert^{3}}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ x(t)\neq0).$$

For this single-label model the distinct-label collision set $\Delta$ of
[[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a) is empty; the excluded point is the
prescribed external-source singularity, not a collision of model labels.

Then every motion of this model is defined for all real times; equivalently,
the maximal interval of every motion is all of $\mathbb R$.
items.strategy: A direct refutation: construct the explicit radial motion r(t)=r_0(1-t/T)^{2/3} for the inverse-square external potential, verify the equation and the stated initial data by differentiation, and show no extension past the finite collision time T exists because a motion would have to pass through the excluded center; the escape alternative of the continuation theorem is exhibited.
items.physical_scope: A refutation, inside the model, of the claim that every motion of the inverse-square external-potential model exists for all real times: for one label with inertial mass $[m]=\mu$ in the external potential $U(x)=-k/|x|$, where $[k]=\mu\ell^{3}\tau^{-2}$, on the external-source-excluded domain, an explicit radial motion with the stated initial data solves the model on $(-\infty,T)$ and has no extension past the finite time $T$, at which the position reaches the excluded center and the speed is unbounded. The item refutes only the all-time-existence claim for this model, illustrates the escape alternative of the breakdown criterion, and asserts no motion of any physical body, no measurement and no empirical claim.
